venue.name: Cineplex Education Cinema
venue.description: Cineplex is a national cinema chain, and its Screenings page is what the site's own footer links to as School Events and Screenings. Under Types of Screenings the page lists Education Cinema, described as alternative programming in Classic Literature, Visual Arts, Opera, Ballet and Film, and it says a group is free to choose any movie, including titles not currently showing in theatres. Bookings go through one inquiry form that asks for a province, a city and a named theatre, and will not accept fewer than 20 guests. Three Cineplex theatres sit on Vancouver Island, two in Victoria and one in Nanaimo, so this entry stands for a company rather than for one place you can drive a bus to.

facility_notes.wheelchair_accessible: Reserved spaces for those requiring mobility devices and their companions, and assistive technology for those who are deaf, hard of hearing, blind, or have low vision.

programs.name: Education Cinema group screening
programs.description: The Screenings page lists Education Cinema as one of three types of screening and describes it as alternative programming in Classic Literature, Visual Arts, Opera, Ballet and Film. A rail of current films sits below it, with the note that a group may choose any movie, including films not currently showing in theatres. Adding pre-ordered concessions, catering, an in-theatre presentation or a reception needs a minimum of 100 guests or a buyout of the smallest auditorium. The inquiry form asks for a preferred date, a start time of morning, afternoon or evening, and a number of guests of at least 20. After it is sent, the site says a team member will reach out to finalise the booking, and that they aim to reply within 3 business days. No price per student, no age or grade range, no running time and no minimum notice period are published.
programs.what_children_do: Sit in a cinema auditorium and watch one film on a big screen, chosen by the group rather than by whatever happens to be showing that week. On the education side the choice runs to classic literature, visual arts, opera, ballet and film.
programs.our_note: Nothing here carries a price, so the only way to learn what a class pays is to send the form and wait for someone to come back to you. Their own form will not accept fewer than 20 guests, so one preschool room on its own is likely too small a group. Decide which cinema you want before you write, because the form asks you to name a province, a city and a theatre, and there are three on the Island.
programs.practical_summary: The whole visit is indoors at a cinema you pick from a list, and an enquiry form is the only way in. No price, no age range, no running time and no notice period are published, and washrooms, lunch space and bus parking are not mentioned at all, so all of that has to be settled with the theatre.
programs.extra_fees_note: The Screenings page prints a beverages and snacks menu running from $11.00 for a small popcorn and a bottled drink to $17.25 for a regular popcorn, a regular fountain drink and candy, and says food choices vary depending on the theatre location.

gaps: no single address — national chain, one row cannot represent multiple cinemas

three Cineplex theatres sit on Vancouver Island: SilverCity Victoria Cinemas at 3130 Tillicum Road, Cineplex Odeon Victoria Cinemas at 780 Yates Street and Galaxy Cinemas Nanaimo at 213-4750 Rutherford Road. Each theatre has its own page with its own address and published coordinates, so this row would be better split into one per cinema

RETRIEVAL NOTE: this site renders in JavaScript and returns only navigation and head metadata to a plain fetch. The page content was read from the site's own __NEXT_DATA__ JSON payload. A fetch-only re-run will appear to find an empty site

the address in the tracker, www.cineplex.com/groupsales, now returns a 404. The old Corporatesales/EducationCinema address redirects to the Parties and Groups page, and the School Events and Screenings link in the site footer points to the Screenings page used here
no price is published anywhere for a school or group screening, per student, per class or per auditorium
no age or grade range is published, so there is nothing to say about how young a group can be
the site never says whether daycare or preschool groups are welcome
no running time is published for a group screening
no minimum notice period is published. The 3 business days on the form is how long they take to reply, not how far ahead a group has to book
the months of the year when group screenings run are unknown; the site does not say
no limit on how many children can come is published. The only figures given are a minimum of 20 guests on the form and a minimum of 100 guests for adding food or a presentation
no chaperone ratio and no free adult places are mentioned

washrooms, indoor lunch space and bus parking are not mentioned for group bookings. Each theatre page carries its own parking line, such as mall or city parkade parking, and none of them mentions buses
no group booking email or phone is published. The only number on the site is a guest services line for the company, which is not a booking route

the Corporate Meetings and Screenings FAQ linked from the Screenings page sits on a separate Cineplex support portal that renders in JavaScript and could not be read, so any price, notice period or age detail it carries is missing here

the page banner photo has no alt text and the social sharing image is the site-wide Cineplex card rather than a photograph, so neither was recorded. The two photos kept here carry the site's own alt text, which is a section label rather than a description of the picture

Cineplex also runs Sensory-Friendly Screenings, described as lights up and sound down, every 4 to 6 weeks on Saturday mornings at the child admission price. Those are public screenings anyone can buy a ticket to, not a group booking, so they are not recorded as a program here
